summary: This tutorial-style video dissects how to process dune imagery and related landscapes in Photoshop and RAW, emphasizing a single “zone” workflow for dunes and a strong visual flow that steers the viewer toward light. The presenter covers foundational decisions (when to preserve a global, single-set adjustment versus multi-zone adjustments), how to create three-dimensionality through tonal and spatial transitions, and a suite of post-processing tools. Key demonstrations include perspective and puppet warps to correct tilt and reshape terrain, simulated wide-angle distortion, color management via selective color and color grading, and the use of non-destructive techniques (history brush, clone stamp, layer duplication) to blend multiple skies and foregrounds. The Milky Way two-shot and Mount Tom sequences illustrate sky-foreground blending, while a final sequence shows noise reduction (Topaz DeNoise AI) and a dramatic blur-plus-luminosity glow to heighten depth. The video also emphasizes process order, non-destructive editing habits, and deliberate edge blending when combining disparate exposures and skies.

sections.title: Dune as One-Zone Subject and Visual Flow
sections.description: Introduction to dunes as one-zone images that respond to a single-wide adjustment. Emphasizes directing the viewer toward the light through three-dimensional transitions, either inward or outward, and discusses why dunes often behave like single-zone subjects for post-processing.

sections.title: Global Adjustments and Edge Behavior
sections.description: Plan to perform broad, image-wide adjustments before more localized edits. Stresses preserving shadow detail while keeping highlights within one stop of blowing out, enabling better control over tonal transitions and color balance.

sections.title: Warping Fundamentals: Perspective Warp to Puppet Warp
sections.description: Describes starting with a perspective warp (up to three boxes) to align shadows and correct tilt, then adds targeted warps to background areas (expanding canvas) and introduces puppet warp as a more dramatic reshaping tool. Emphasizes maintaining recognizability of dunes while achieving the desired composition.

sections.title: Distortion Tools: Simulating Wide Angles with RAW/Filter
sections.description: Demonstrates how to emulate wide-angle distortion using the Distort and Camera Raw Filter (adaptive wide-angle) and discusses edge stretching versus center scaling, with notes on maintaining content integrity for both wide and telephoto perspectives.

sections.title: Color Management: Selective Color and Color Grading
sections.description: Shows color corrections to fix problematic yellows and other areas by neutralizing color in RAW, then rebuilding color through targeted selective color and color grading to preserve a cohesive color palette across the image.

sections.title: Milky Way Two-Shot Blend and Mount Tom Sky Integration
sections.description: Outlines blending two exposures (foreground and sky) for Milky Way shots, including selecting compatible foreground skies, maintaining horizon color consistency, and using clone-stamp/sky-blend techniques to integrate a secondary sky (Mount Tom) into the final composition.

sections.title: Sky Integration Techniques: Sky Warps and Cloud Adjustments
sections.description: Details how to warp sky regions to create stronger leading lines toward the mountain, using trapezoid rules and puppet warp to shape clouds, followed by blending and edge-smoothing to ensure natural transitions.

sections.title: Layered Lighting and Foreground Emphasis
sections.description: Explains layering brighter foreground and darker background layers, then painting in glow and luminosity to heighten depth, followed by selective adjustments to keep blues balanced while emphasizing light direction.

sections.title: Final Glow, Non-Destructive Saving, and Versioning
sections.description: Culminates with a strong glow via blur plus luminosity, final color and edge refinements, and practical advice on saving multiple versions (versioned PSDs/TIFFs) to preserve different stages of editing and facilitate non-destructive revisits.
